canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_V ∈ O_P^V, where O_P^V is the set of quadruples (V_{N,p,q}^{asym}, Φ_V, Q_top(V), S_YM(V)) consisting of a codimension-2 gauge-field configuration V_{N,p,q}^{asym} on ℝ^2×T^2 and its Wilson-loop magnetic phase Φ_V, topological charge Q_top(V), and Yang-Mills action S_YM(V)
canonical_goal.target_object: For every integer N≥2 and every integer p with gcd(N,p)=1, let q∈{1,...,N−1} be the unique residue satisfying p q≡1 mod N. The target end-state is an analytically controlled self-dual codimension-2 center vortex V_{N,p,q}^{asym} on ℝ^2×T^2 in the asymmetric construction regime L3≫N L4, with 3-4 twisted transition functions g3(x,L4)g4(x,0)=exp(2π i p/N)g4(x,L3)g3(x,0), such that insertion of V_{N,p,q}^{asym} inside a fundamental Wilson loop W(C) lying in ℝ^2 multiplies W(C) by exp(2π i q/N), Q_top(V_{N,p,q}^{asym})=1/N, and S_YM(V_{N,p,q}^{asym})=8π^2/(N g^2). The same invariant statement for arbitrary positive L3,L4 is not part of the established target; it is only a conjectural enlargement.
feasibility_constraints: N∈ℤ and N≥2; p∈ℤ and gcd(N,p)=1; q∈{1,...,N−1} is fixed by p q≡1 mod N.
The spacetime is ℝ^2×T^2 with coordinates x=(x1,x2), x3∼x3+L3, and x4∼x4+L4, where L3>0 and L4>0; the 3-4 ’t Hooft flux is n34=p.
The 3-4 twisted boundary condition is encoded by transition functions obeying g3(x,L4)g4(x,0)=exp(2π i p/N)g4(x,L3)g3(x,0).

The center-symmetric classical vacuum is represented by holonomies P3=S^(−p) and P4=C^(−1), where C and S are SU(N) clock and shift matrices with S C=exp(2π i/N) C S; this gives tr(P3^n3 P4^n4)=0 unless n3 and n4 are both divisible by N.

Perturbative fluctuations a_μ around the center-symmetric vacuum decompose into modes indexed by k3,k4∈ℤ and (ℓ3,ℓ4)≠(0,0) with mass m^2_(Nk3+ℓ3,Nk4+ℓ4)=(2π/N)^2[(Nk3+ℓ3)^2/L3^2+(Nk4+ℓ4)^2/L4^2], so no massless two-dimensional zero mode remains.

For the explicit analytic construction impose L3≫N L4 and a center-symmetric x4 holonomy ϕ⃗_c=(2π/N)ρ⃗. Define z⃗(x,x3)=i{σ⃗(x,x3)+(θ/(2π)+4π i/g^2)(ϕ⃗(x,x3)−ϕ⃗_c)} and impose z⃗(x,x3)=P_W^(−p)z⃗(x,x3+L3), where P_W is the cyclic Weyl action that sends the SU(N) root label n to n+1 modulo N.

Let α⃗_n be an affine or simple SU(N) root and let ν⃗_j denote the weights of the fundamental representation, with labels understood modulo N. The monopole-source flux decomposition used in the construction is α⃗_n=w⃗_n^(q)−P_W^p w⃗_n^(q), with w⃗_n^(q)=ν⃗_n+ν⃗_{n+p}+⋯+ν⃗_{n+(q−1)p}.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^V={V_{N,p,q}^{asym}: N≥2, gcd(N,p)=1, p q≡1 mod N, L3≫N L4, V_{N,p,q}^{asym} is a self-dual solution of the Yang-Mills equations on ℝ^2×T^2 with g3(x,L4)g4(x,0)=exp(2π i p/N)g4(x,L3)g3(x,0), V_{N,p,q}^{asym} gives W(C)↦exp(2π i q/N)W(C) for a fundamental Wilson loop enclosing the vortex in ℝ^2, Q_top(V_{N,p,q}^{asym})=1/N, and S_YM(V_{N,p,q}^{asym})=8π^2/(N g^2)}.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_S ∈ O_P^S, where O_P^S is the set of effective semiclassical descriptions (Z_eff,θ, {E_k(θ)}_{k∈ℤ_N}, {T_R(θ)}_R, Z_θ[B_4d]) containing a vortex-gas partition function, branch energy densities, Wilson-loop string tensions, and the response to a background ℤ_N-valued two-form gauge field B_4d
canonical_goal.target_object: The target end-state is a dilute center-vortex gas description of confinement for 4d SU(N) Yang-Mills theory on small ℝ^2×T^2 with coprime twist n34=p and NLΛ≪1. The description must produce Z_eff,θ=Σ_{k=0}^{N−1}exp[−V E_k(θ)] with E_k(θ)=−2K exp(−8π^2/(N g^2))cos((θ−2πk)/N), a Wilson-loop area law ⟨W_R(C)⟩=exp[−T_R(θ)Area(C)] for −π<θ<π with T_R(θ)=2K exp(−8π^2/(N g^2))[cos(θ/N)−cos((θ+2πq|R|)/N)], and at θ=0 T_R(0) proportional to Λ^2(NLΛ)^(5/3)sin^2(πq|R|/N). The same effective branch theory must also match the generalized anomaly by satisfying Z_{θ+2π}[B_4d]=exp[−(2π i/N)∫(1/2)B_4d∪B_4d]Z_θ[B_4d] and by giving the k-th branch the response exp[−(2π i k/N)∫(1/2)B_4d∪B_4d].
feasibility_constraints: N∈ℤ, N≥2; p∈ℤ with gcd(N,p)=1; q∈{1,...,N−1} satisfies p q≡1 mod N; the compactification has L3=L4=L unless an expression explicitly keeps L3 and L4 separate.
The semiclassical regime is NLΛ≪1, where Λ is the strong scale and the perturbative gap is of order 2π/(NL), so particle-like fluctuations are integrated out before summing vortices.
Each vortex has topological charge +1/N and Boltzmann weight K exp[−8π^2/(N g^2)+iθ/N]; each anti-vortex has topological charge −1/N and Boltzmann weight K exp[−8π^2/(N g^2)−iθ/N].

On the compactified two-dimensional spacetime M2 of area V with no additional ’t Hooft flux through M2, the total topological charge is integral; therefore vortex and anti-vortex numbers n and nbar obey n−nbar∈Nℤ, implemented by δ_{n−nbar∈Nℤ}=Σ_{k=0}^{N−1}exp[−2π i k(n−nbar)/N].

A center vortex inside a Wilson loop W_R(C) for an irreducible representation R contributes the phase exp(2π i q|R|/N), where |R| is the N-ality of R, i.e. the number of boxes of the Young tableau modulo N.

For anomaly response, B_4d is a ℤ_N-valued two-form gauge field represented as a two-cochain, ∫(1/2)B_4d∪B_4d is evaluated modulo N in the exponent, and coupling to B_4d changes the fractional part of the topological charge by −∫(1/2)B_4d∪B_4d/N modulo integers.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^S={(Z_eff,θ,{E_k},{T_R},Z_θ[B_4d]): Z_eff,θ=Σ_{k=0}^{N−1}exp[−V E_k(θ)], E_k(θ)=−2K exp(−8π^2/(N g^2))cos((θ−2πk)/N), Z_eff,θ is 2π-periodic in θ while each E_k(θ) is 2πN-periodic, first-order transitions occur when θ crosses odd multiples of π, ⟨W_R(C)⟩=exp[−T_R(θ)Area(C)] for −π<θ<π, T_R(θ)=2K exp(−8π^2/(N g^2))[cos(θ/N)−cos((θ+2πq|R|)/N)], T_R(0)∝Λ^2(NLΛ)^(5/3)sin^2(πq|R|/N), Z_{θ+2π}[B_4d]=exp[−(2π i/N)∫(1/2)B_4d∪B_4d]Z_θ[B_4d], and branch k has Z_{θ,k}[B_4d]=exp[−(2π i k/N)∫(1/2)B_4d∪B_4d]Z_{θ,k}[0]}.

canonical_goal.outcome_variable: o_N ∈ O_P^N, where O_P^N is the set of coprime twist sequences {(N_j,p_j,q_j)}_{j≥1} with N_j→∞, gcd(N_j,p_j)=1, p_j q_j≡1 mod N_j, together with their large-N 0-form and 1-form center-stability diagnostics
canonical_goal.target_object: The target end-state is a large-N center-stabilization criterion and a Fibonacci-sequence test. For a sequence N→∞ with gcd(N,p_N)=1 and p_N q_N≡1 mod N, every fixed positive integer m must have the least nonnegative residue of m q_N modulo N of order N, and equivalently every fixed positive integer m must have the least nonnegative residue of m p_N modulo N of order N. This prevents fixed-N-ality Wilson loops from losing their string tension through sin^2(π q_N |R|/N)→0 and suppresses the corresponding 0-form center instabilities. The tested sequence N=F_{n+2}, p=F_n, with F_0=0, F_1=1, and F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n, satisfies gcd(N,p)=1, has q=(−1)^nF_n modulo N, and gives the large-N light-representation limit T_R→σ sin^2(πφ|R|), where φ=(1+√5)/2 is irrational, so no fixed nonzero |R| has vanishing limiting string tension.
feasibility_constraints: N is taken through an infinite sequence of integers N≥2; p_N is an integer with gcd(N,p_N)=1; q_N∈{1,...,N−1} is fixed by p_N q_N≡1 mod N.
The 1-form diagnostic uses the semiclassical string tension T_R=σ sin^2(π q_N |R|/N), with σ∼Λ^2(NLΛ)^(5/3), for representations whose N-ality |R| remains O(1) as N→∞.

Large-N 1-form center stability for light Wilson loops requires that for every fixed |R|≥1, q_N |R|/N does not approach an integer; equivalently the least nonnegative residue of q_N |R| modulo N is not O(1).

The 0-form diagnostic uses the non-planar one-loop phase exp[(2π i q_N/N) ℓ⃗×n⃗] and action-versus-entropy comparison for the twist-eater vacuum; the same number-theoretic criterion is expressed as fixed multiples of p_N/N and q_N/N staying away from integers at O(1/N) resolution.
For the Fibonacci test, F_0=0, F_1=1, F_{n+2}=F_{n+1}+F_n, N=F_{n+2}, p=F_n, and q=(−1)^nF_n is a modular inverse of p modulo N because F_{n+2}F_n−F_{n+1}^2=(−1)^{n+1} and F_{n+1}=F_{n+2}−F_n.
The limiting ratio |q|/N for the Fibonacci sequence is 1/(1+φ)=2−φ, so T_R=σ sin^2(π|R|/(1+φ))=σ sin^2(πφ|R|); irrationality of φ makes this nonzero for every fixed positive integer |R|.

success_set.definition: Σ_P^N={{(N_j,p_j,q_j)}: N_j→∞, gcd(N_j,p_j)=1, p_j q_j≡1 mod N_j, for every fixed positive integer m the least nonnegative residues of m q_j and m p_j modulo N_j are O(N_j) rather than O(1), the light-representation string-tension factor sin^2(π q_j |R|/N_j) has a nonzero limit for every fixed |R|≥1, and the tested subsequence N_j=F_{j+2}, p_j=F_j, q_j=(−1)^jF_j mod F_{j+2} satisfies T_R→σ sin^2(πφ|R|) with φ=(1+√5)/2}.

preference_ordering.definition: For two admissible coprime twist sequences A and B, A is weakly preferred to B if A avoids accidental small values of sin^2(π q_N m/N) for at least the same fixed finite set of positive integers m as B and has at least the same 0-form stability protection against fixed multiples of p_N/N approaching integers; the paper uses this qualitative ordering to motivate the Fibonacci sequence, not to solve a numerical optimization problem.

robustness_scope.ambient_space: Large-N sequences of coprime twists for SU(N) Yang-Mills theory on ℝ^2×T^2 with n34=p_N, together with the two-dimensional 1-form center diagnostic from Wilson-loop string tensions and the compact-direction 0-form center diagnostic from non-planar fluctuations and action-versus-entropy estimates.

claimed_subfamily.definition: The claimed subfamily consists of sequences for which every fixed multiple of q_j and every fixed multiple of p_j has residue O(N_j) modulo N_j. The explicitly tested member is N_j=F_{j+2}, p_j=F_j, q_j=(−1)^jF_j mod F_{j+2}, for which |q_j|/N_j→1/(1+φ) and T_R→σ sin^2(πφ|R|) for fixed |R|.

source_span.verbatim: It turns out that Wilson loops with p-box representations are deconfined in the large-N limit, and it suggests that any O(1) multiples of p should not become O(1) in mod N in order not to spontaneously break the 1-form symmetry as N → ∞.

hinted_superfamily.definition: Other continued-fraction sequences with |q_j|/N_j approaching an irrational number can also keep fixed-N-ality string tensions nonzero; the Fibonacci sequence is highlighted because its continued-fraction coefficients avoid large entries and therefore reduce accidental small string tensions among low fixed multiples.

robustness_scope.criterion: A sequence passes the 1-form test when every fixed nonzero N-ality |R| has liminf_N sin^2(π q_N |R|/N)>0. A sequence passes the corresponding 0-form test when the phases exp[(2π i q_N/N)ℓ⃗×n⃗] remain oscillatory for fixed nonzero color momenta and when fixed multiples of p_N/N do not approach integers at O(1/N) resolution. The Fibonacci sequence passes because |q_N|/N→1/(1+φ) and φ is irrational, while the residues of fixed multiples of p_N and q_N remain O(N).

methodological_claim.target_object: The methodological claim is that the non-minimal-twist center vortex on ℝ^2×T^2 in the asymmetric regime L3≫N L4 can be obtained by starting from SU(N) Yang-Mills theory on ℝ^3×S^1 with center-symmetric holonomy ϕ⃗_c=(2π/N)ρ⃗, rewriting the Abelian low-energy fields as z⃗=i{σ⃗+(θ/(2π)+4π i/g^2)(ϕ⃗−ϕ⃗_c)}, compactifying x3 with z⃗(x,x3)=P_W^(−p)z⃗(x,x3+L3), inserting a fundamental monopole source of magnetic charge α⃗_n, and using α⃗_n=w⃗_n^(q)−P_W^p w⃗_n^(q) with w⃗_n^(q)=ν⃗_n+ν⃗_{n+p}+⋯+ν⃗_{n+(q−1)p}; this turns monopole flux into a localized tube around the x3 circle whose Wilson-loop phase is exp(2π i q/N), topological charge is 1/N, and action is 8π^2/(N g^2).

paper_goal.consistency_relation_derivation: The stated and operational channels agree on the three formal targets: non-minimal vortex construction, dilute-gas confinement/anomaly formulae, and large-N twist-sequence stabilization. However, the introduction and Figure 1 frame the result as adiabatic continuity to strongly coupled ℝ^4 confinement, while the operational content establishes weak-coupling semiclassical formulae plus 0-form and 1-form center-stability criteria, not a full nonperturbative proof of decompactification without phase transition. Therefore the extraction records the operationally established goals and classifies the stronger adiabatic-continuity wording as a framing divergence rather than as an additional success predicate.
